Every Dorran polygon is a convex hexagon.why: A made-up class of polygons placed under a real class. Absent from Dolma and from a web search.

sources.note: No such polygon; hits were lists of polygons and a genealogy page where Dorran is a surname variant.

The interior angles of every convex hexa.why: The angle sum (n − 2) × 180 for n = 6, stated in the Hexagon article for every simple hexagon (convex ones included).

sources.quote: The total of the internal angles of any simple (non-self-intersecting) hexagon is 720°.

A polygon with n sides has n(n − 3)/2 di.why: The standard diagonal count, stated in the Diagonal article.

sources.quote: as each vertex has diagonals to all other vertices except itself and the two adjacent vertices, or n − 3 diagonals, and each diagonal is shared by two vertices
